thread:
mike: FYI customer 'AGT' hit a burst-of-traffic 429 last night during an email campaign. They say it was a short spike (~45s) but we returned rate_limited and burst credits dropped to 0. Can we confirm behavior and next steps?

jess: Sorry to hear — can you paste the response headers and a short repro curl? usually X-RateLimit headers help.

mike: Pasting redacted response below:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 12
X-Burst-Credits-Remaining: 0
X-Burst-Credits-Replenish-Seconds: 360
{ "error": "rate_limited", "message": "burst credits exhausted" }
```
Customer curl they used (sanitized):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" -d '{"prompt":"...","max_tokens":200}'
```
They said traffic is spiky: 300 reqs in 40s, then quiet.

lee: Thanks — that matches the short-burst token-bucket we're using. Quick summary: accounts are given a steady refill rate + a small burst pool. Short spikes consume burst credits; if pool hits 0 you get 429s until it refills. Refill happens over minutes (configurable by tier).

lee: Workarounds we can offer immediately: 1) Recommend client-side smoothing (leaky bucket client) + exponential backoff with jitter on 429s. 2) If they expect repeated short spikes, suggest Dedicated or a higher-tier burst policy so pool size and refill rate increase. 3) Short-term: route can be set to a lower-cost model variant concurrently to reduce token consumption during spikes.

maya: Customer asked if burst credits top-up faster during quiet periods — yes but it's capped by the refill rate. We should also check if their account had any concurrent heavy usage (embeddings jobs etc.) eating credits.

mike: I looked at their usage graph — embeddings batch job did run at the same hour (overlapping). I'll ask them to stagger. They want to know if we can adjust smoothing policy for them while we investigate.

jess: We can apply a temporary policy tweak for accounts in edge cases. Need Eng sign-off to change refill/size. Lee, can we do a soft tweak for AGT (account id AGT-234) for the next 24h?

lee: I can increase the burst pool by 3x for 24h on canary infra, but I need a ticket with business justification (customer name, expected QPS and spike profile). Also note: this only masks the root cause if they keep doing sustained spikes.

mike: I'll open a ticket and ask customer for exact spike CSV (timestamp,qps). Also sending them a short client-side snippet:
```js
// very small leaky-bucket example
let tokens = 10; // initial small bucket for client smoothing
setInterval(() => { tokens = Math.min(tokens + 1, 10); }, 1000); // refill 1/s
function send(req) { if (tokens <= 0) return retryLater(req); tokens--; return fetch(req); }
```

maya: I'll notify AM and offer to schedule a quick call to walk them through staggering, retry strategy, and the Dedicated option. :phone: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Applied canary tweak for AGT-234 on infra-canary-3 (burst_pool_multiplier=3) — change id = cs-8892 — TTL 24h.

jess: Thanks. Follow-up items: 1) Mike to collect spike CSV and open support ticket. 2) Lee to monitor canary metrics and revert if any instability. 3) Maya to set up customer call. 4) Eng-runtime to consider whether we should expose a self-serve "burst smoothing" knob in Console.

mike: On it. I'll update thread when ticket is created. :white_check_mark:
